steps.label: Prompt
steps.text:
Make a 30-second launch film for [your product], 16:9 at 1920x1080, 30 fps.

Before you design anything, learn the product: read [your product URL], and the codebase if you have it. Write down in one line what it does and who it is for, list its three strongest features, and show me that summary first.

Story:
1. Hook, first second: one bold line or image that names the problem [your product] solves.
2. Meet the product: its real interface, logo, colours and type. No generic mockups.
3. Three beats, one per feature: show it working and give it one short line of copy, under eight words.
4. End card: logo, one-line promise and [your product URL].

Look and motion: modern SaaS launch style, like the best YC launch videos: a clean canvas, the product's own accent colour, crisp kinetic type, springy UI transitions and quick zooms into the interface.

Use the product's real screenshots, logo and assets, but never as raw images: break them into components and icons so each piece can be animated.
Make the motion juicy and make it follow the music: every move lands on a beat. This should look like a professional production, not a demo or a prototype.

Sound: compose a short original track in code, or use a royalty-free one and tell me where it is from. Give every cut and reveal its own sound effect, land the cuts on the beat, and mix so nothing clips.

How to build it: draw every frame in code as a pure function of time (HTML, Canvas or SVG, Remotion or HyperFrames all work), render the frames headlessly and assemble an MP4 with the audio. Then watch your render at full speed and fix anything that feels slow, cramped, generic or off-brand before you hand it over.

original.label: Prompt
original.text: Make a dynamic 30-second motion graphics video that shows what an incredible motion designer you are, like it's your showreel for a résumé. go all out.  Make it a video to introduce https://mdfor.dev Use actual product screenshot/logo/assets Must have music and motion must match the music  Do it like a real professional production video, not like a demo or prototype. Add more animation and motion design; avoid using screenshots as raw; instead, break them down into components/icons so we can animate those too. Make the motions more juicy. Use the best motion design techniques you can.
